shared_context: Read summary/group_meeting_notes.md first. PI-verified facts: A_n is purely imaginary (A_n = i*a_n); overall frequency scaling dimension is 2n-4; n=4 is finite but singular at the exact on-shell point (oracle SIGFPEs/NaNs there) and must be obtained by a delta->0 limit (refs: omega=(-3,1,3,-1)->-24 i, omega=(-5,2,5,-2)->-320 i); n=7 exact is slow, use --double. Reference table is in the notes.

tasks.title: Build a clean A_n dataset and discover the closed form empirically
tasks.description: Build your own copy of the oracle and generate a comprehensive, exact-rational dataset of A_n in the two-minus sector for n = 5, 6 (exact) and n = 7 (use --double), over many in-sector kinematic points, including extreme/non-generic regimes (one frequency much larger or much smaller than the rest) and also several n=4 points obtained by the delta->0 limit method (see notes). Then mine this dataset for the closed form: (a) confirm/refine the scaling dimension (2n-4) and the purely-imaginary property; (b) determine the exact symmetry group of a_n (which permutations of legs leave it invariant -- handle the minus legs {1,2} vs plus legs {3..n} separately, and remember omega_2 is a minus leg in the -w parametrization); (c) determine the analytic nature of a_n as a function of the omega_i -- is it a polynomial or a rational function, what is its degree, and what are its poles/zeros (factor the exact rationals to expose structure); (d) using these constraints, fit/guess an explicit closed-form candidate a_n({omega_i}) and test it against the oracle. Try expressing a_n in terms of natural building blocks (products of frequencies, elementary symmetric polynomials, the |k_i| = omega_i^2, partial sums of omega over subsets, the pairwise structure seen at n=4).
deliverables: data/ : exact-rational amplitude tables (csv or yaml) for n=4(limit),5,6,7 with the full omega vector and a_n for each point; include the kinematics generator script in code/.
A written empirical-structure report (derivations/ note) covering scaling, symmetry, polynomial-vs-rational character, degree, and factorization of a_n.
A best candidate closed-form for a_n with residuals vs ./bg at n=4(limit),5,6,7 (>=3 points each incl. one extreme regime), relative error reported.
Registered claims/figures/decisions with stable s1_* IDs and a session report JSON.
tasks.notes: If you reach a candidate that passes at all n you tested, register it clearly with the exact points + residuals so the PI can re-verify. If not, report the strongest partial structure (e.g. the exact degree and symmetry) so round 2 can build on it. Do not redo work settled in the group notes -- build on it.

tasks.title: Derive the closed form analytically from the Berends-Giele recursion
tasks.description: Work analytically from the recursion implemented in bg.cpp (EKernel, FKernel, Vertex, Propagator, BGCurrent, BGAmplitude) to derive the structure of A_n in the two-minus sector. Concretely: (1) Carry out the recursion symbolically (by hand and/or with sympy) for n=4 and n=5 in the two-minus sector to get a_n as an explicit closed expression in the omega_i, exposing why the result is purely imaginary and where the n=4 {2,4} 0/0 cancels in the full amplitude (this explains why A_4 is finite). (2) Identify which diagrams/partitions dominate and how the kernels simplify when the signs are fixed to (-1,-1,+1,...,+1). (3) From the n=4,5 closed expressions, conjecture the general A_n and write it explicitly as a function of {omega_1,...,omega_n}. (4) Test the conjecture against the oracle at n=4 (limit),5,6,7, multiple points each including a non-generic regime, to <=1e-10 relative error. Use the PI's reference values in the group notes as immediate checks while deriving (e.g. n=4 -> -24 i and -320 i; n=5 (2,3,5) -> -3328 i).
deliverables: derivations/ : a clear derivation of a_4 and a_5 from the BG recursion (symbolic), and the argument for the purely-imaginary result and the n=4 finiteness.
An explicit conjectured closed-form A_n({omega}) with the reasoning that produced it.
Numerical verification table vs ./bg at n=4(limit),5,6,7 (>=3 points each incl. one extreme regime) with relative residuals; scratch code in code/.
Registered claims/figures/decisions with stable s2_* IDs and a session report JSON.
tasks.notes: You and student-1 are working independently toward the same goal from different angles (theory vs data) -- that redundancy is intentional and gives a cross-check. If you obtain a passing candidate, register it with exact points + residuals for PI re-verification. If only partial, report the exact symbolic a_4/a_5 -- those alone are valuable for round 2.
